seivalue.title: SeiValue Test
seivalue.subtitle: A fandom test for Japanese voice-actress fans v2.0
seivalue.intro: 4 axes and a large question pool drawn at random, placing you on the Japanese voice-actress fandom map. In the end you get your school of thought, a rarity, an honest community verdict, and voice actresses you may like.
seivalue.guide: Five options per statement: strongly agree, agree, neutral, disagree, strongly disagree. The more extreme you are, the further the axis tilts. A few trap statements are hidden inside - answer too consistently and you may unlock a secret result.

fast.name: Quick test · 32 items
fast.desc: A result in about three minutes. Good for a casual run.

pro.name: PRO mode · 64 items
pro.desc: Exactly twice the length, more contradiction pairs and traps, so the four axes land closer to your real leanings.

report.title: SeiValue Fun Report Card
report.subtitle: Seiyuu Intel Station · Voice-Actress Fan Test

aesr.name: Generous Free-Riding Evangelist
aesr.desc: Only acting matters, you preach to everyone and praise everyone — while your wallet stays welded shut. Pure love, free of charge.
aesr.review: Community verdict: nobody dislikes you, and almost nobody actually got converted by you. You prove free love is sustainable.

aesp.name: Acting Purist Patron
aesp.desc: You praise the craft while quietly swiping your card. If she never got famous, that is the industry problem.
aesp.review: Community verdict: the best-reputed type. Money and taste in one package, though sales charts still make you sigh.

aedr.name: Free-Riding Reviewer
aedr.desc: Harshest reviews, busiest preaching, cheapest spending. You point out the problems, others pay for them.
aedr.review: Community verdict: loudest in the review threads, quietest at the checkout. You call it honesty, others call it nitpicking.

aedp.name: Paying Roaster
aedp.desc: Taste plus cash flow. The only problem is that your roasting always happens after checkout.
aedp.review: Community verdict: one mouth, two wallets. The kind of user agencies adore - roast by day, pay by night.

aqsr.name: Cellar Archaeologist
aqsr.desc: Digging alone in a corner until 3 a.m. Do not disturb her private time with you. Free, but sacred.
aqsr.review: Community verdict: never seen in public, yet half the archives in the fandom look like your work. Anti-social, but professional.

aqsp.name: Basement Patron
aqsp.desc: No preaching, no socialising, no fellow fans allowed — and the bill is still paid in full every month.
aqsp.review: Community verdict: the legendary anonymous patron. No posts, no noise, just a name somewhere in the sales rankings.

aqdr.name: Forum Veteran with a Yellow Badge
aqdr.desc: Badge in hand, watching since her debut, you have seen every kind of monster. Do not argue with a veteran.
aqdr.review: Community verdict: honorary citizen of the forums. Your signature is longer than other people threads, and seniority is your weapon.

aqdp.name: Appraiser and ATM
aqdp.desc: Debunking with one hand, renewing with the other. Your mouth says not good enough, your finger is already on pay.
aqdp.review: Community verdict: you sneer and you subscribe. Others call it armchair spending, you call it professional support.

fesr.name: Free-Riding Face Fan
fesr.desc: In for the looks, preaching to everyone, furious at any doubt — but not spending a cent.
fesr.review: Community verdict: in through the face, out through the wallet. Your loudest devotion is also your quietest bank statement.

fesp.name: Idol War Veteran
fesp.desc: A veteran who fought through every idol project. Your youth, your glow sticks and your money all stayed at the venue.
fesp.review: Community verdict: an old guard of the idol-project era. You are not following a person, you are following an epoch.

fedr.name: Professional Nuisance
fedr.desc: Burning passion when preaching, a scalpel when debunking, and never a coin spent. The nuisance itself.
fedr.review: Community verdict: passion and being insufferable are one step apart, and you dance on that line. Fans fear you; agencies fear you more.

fedp.name: Flame-War Essayist
fedp.desc: Paying while writing essays, first into every flame war, and always the one who gets the bill.
fedp.review: Community verdict: a trending-topic regular. Money and keyboard both flying, so nobody can tell which side you are on.

fqsr.name: Romantic Free-Rider
fqsr.desc: Looks only, mine only, all praise, zero spending. A perfectly self-sufficient loop.
fqsr.review: Community verdict: one person sustaining an entire private universe, almost for free. Calm immersion, sudden jumpscare.

fqsp.name: Dream-Girl ATM
fqsp.desc: The final form of the dream girl: she stays inside the fence, your money does not.
fqsp.review: Community verdict: she never leaves the fence, your money never stays inside. A fandom legend that only the sales chart remembers.

fqdr.name: No-Fellow-Fans Free-Rider
fqdr.desc: Fellow fans are enemies, not paying is a principle, looks are the only standard. The sole judge of your own small world.
fqdr.review: Community verdict: your world is you and her, and you are not paying either. Approaching is harassment, and you would not pay for that anyway.

fqdp.name: Paying Landmine Girl
fqdp.desc: Paying, fencing and debunking in one package. You curse the hardest, pay the most, and let nobody near your oshi.
fqdp.review: Community verdict: loudest criticism, biggest payments, zero tolerance for other opinions. Fellow fans quietly leave the group chat.

voice.left: You follow the craft itself: voice, breath and emotional range are your only yardstick.
voice.right: You follow the person: face, aura and camera presence weigh as much as ability.

consume.left: You believe liking something does not require paying: free streams, second-hand and sales are all legitimate.
consume.right: You believe money is the proof of sincerity: discs, merch and live tickets are part of the support.

community.left: You are a born broadcaster, pulling everyone you know into the pit with you.
community.right: You prefer your own small room; a bigger crowd dilutes what you love.

interact.left: Your tolerance for her is almost infinite, and criticism makes you block for her first.
interact.right: You keep a clear distance: you roast, you debunk, and you hate being swept up by feelings.

voice.left: Acclaimed for acting within their projects, with a filmography deep enough to dig for years
voice.right: The camera-facing face of idol projects — looks and stage presence at once

consume.left: Huge output — their works are everywhere in anime and games, free to enjoy
consume.right: Long-running staples of idol projects and live stages, worth the tribute

community.left: Endless radio and variety content, enough material to preach every day
community.right: A small, tight-knit project with a cooler aura that suits slow solo research

interact.left: A long-stable gentle image that is very hard to attack
interact.right: A tough aura and solid craft, so roasting them never feels risky

rt1.name: Same-Oshi-Hating Landmine
rt1.review: Verdict: loves hardest, curses loudest, pays nothing. Fellow fans block you first, passers-by cross the street.

rt2.name: Seniority-Waving Fan
rt2.review: Verdict: watching since her debut, and your main job is telling others they arrived too late. Deep archives, foul tone.

rt3.name: Chart-Data Grinder
rt3.review: Verdict: sales, rankings and hashtag numbers are your religion. You may not love her - you love the rising curve.

rt4.name: Free-Riding Materialist
rt4.review: Verdict: not a cent spent, yet you know her credits better than her agency does. Data-team energy, hardest to please.

rt5.name: Unconditional Yes Patriarch
rt5.review: Verdict: in your eyes she has no flaws, only bad days. Others bring evidence, you bring filters.

rt6.name: Looks-First Romance Brain
rt6.review: Verdict: acting is nice, but can you eat it? Your comments come in two sentences: beautiful, and beautiful.

rt7.name: Anti-Idol Acting Purist
rt7.review: Verdict: you frown at photobooks and sigh at variety shows. You do not dislike her - you want her locked in the recording booth.

rt8.name: Dream-Girl Shield
rt8.review: Verdict: she is yours, cameras are redundant, other fans are trespassing. The hardest type to talk to, and never stingy.

rt9.name: Flame-War Longform Writer
rt9.review: Verdict: one post, three thousand words of analysis. You call it objective; others call it a microscope with an agenda.

rt10.name: Casting Conspiracy Theorist
rt10.review: Verdict: she was skipped, so someone must be suppressing her. You know every cast list and every conspiracy.

rt11.name: Live-Show Romance Brain
rt11.review: Verdict: the better the view, the deeper the fall, the faster the card. The concert ends and the bill and tears arrive together.

rt12.name: Idol-Apologist Tribute Party
rt12.review: Verdict: when she stays quiet you feel wronged, when she performs you forgive instantly. Wallet and filter open together, no discounts.

rt13.name: One-Oshi Fanatic
rt13.review: Verdict: one oshi, one dead end. Others call multi-oshi cheating; your loyalty looks like guarding a tomb.

rt14.name: Overposting Evangelist
rt14.review: Verdict: everything you enjoy becomes a recommendation, ignored ten times, delivered an eleventh. Easiest person to mute.

eggDesc.e_all_agree: All thirty-three statements strongly agreed. Your worldview has no word for disagree.
eggDesc.e_all_disagree: Thirty-three strong disagreements. You came here to tear the place down.
eggDesc.e_chaos: Fast, chaotic and full of contradictions — you did not come to take a test, you came to wreck it.
eggDesc.e_toilet: You stepped on every trap statement while all four axes stayed in the middle. A true patriarch.
eggDesc.e_left: All four axes pinned to the left. Purity that is hard to beat.
eggDesc.e_right: All four axes pinned to the right. The ultimate devotee of tributes and idols.
eggDesc.e_void: You skipped more than half the test and stayed neutral on the rest. Just passing through.
eggDesc.e_blaster: One third strongly agree, one third strongly disagree, one third neutral — answered in seconds.
eggDesc.e_multi_chaos: Completely random choices, yet all four axes sit dead centre. The will of the chaos god.
eggDesc.e_sprint: Thirty-three statements clicked in one go, less than two seconds each.
eggDesc.e_pendulum: Agree, disagree, agree, disagree — your answers swing like a metronome.
eggDesc.e_contradict: More than five self-contradictions. At least one of them is your true feeling.
eggDesc.e_fishing: You stepped on four or more trap statements while keeping your position dead centre. Suspicious.
eggDesc.e_all_neutral: Neutral on every single one. Congratulations, you are the void itself.
eggDesc.e_random: Randomness above 90 percent. You were basically clicking with your eyes closed.
eggDesc.e_blank: You skipped more than a fifth of the test, which makes the rest more precious.
eggDesc.e_middle: All four axes hug the centre line. You are more neutral than you thought.

questions.q01: Whatever project my oshi takes on, I support it unconditionally.
questions.q02: Following several voice actresses in one season is perfectly normal.
questions.q03: A voice actress private life is none of my business; I only care about her acting and her works.
questions.q04: I buy discs and merch because the works themselves deserve it.
questions.q05: When someone bashes my oshi, I will absolutely argue back.
questions.q06: A voice actress turning idol is putting the cart before the horse.
questions.q07: Radio shows and interviews that have nothing to do with characters, I basically never click.
questions.q08: Chart positions do not matter; as long as I like it, that is enough.
questions.q09: I want more fellow fans; the more people, the livelier it gets.
questions.q10: As long as I understand my oshi, that is fine — I do not want more people to find her.
questions.q11: A voice actress with a striking face draws me in more easily.
questions.q12: I can enjoy her works without paying a cent, and I know I do not owe her a tribute.
questions.q13: I prefer chatting in a small circle of friends rather than making noise in public.
questions.q14: Her happiness matters more than anything; I rarely pick at her faults.
questions.q15: Even if her face never appears on screen, if the acting is good enough I can follow her for life.
questions.q16: If she is in it, I will buy the limited edition no matter the price.
questions.q17: Even if my oshi stepped on my face, I would still find it cute.
questions.q18: Chart numbers decide whether my oshi has any value.
questions.q19: The best part of being a fan is preaching her to everyone around me.
questions.q20: I roast my oshi more often than I praise her.
questions.q21: A bad project is a bad project; if my oshi took it, I will still call it out.
questions.q22: Liking several at once is cheating; you should be loyal to one.
questions.q23: If the radio mentions anything private, I immediately want to clip it and keep it.
questions.q24: As long as it is my oshi, I will buy three copies even if the acting is wooden.
questions.q25: I never join arguments in the community — too much hassle.
questions.q26: Live stages and photobooks are the real thing; what is wrong with going idol?
questions.q27: I listen to every single episode of my oshi radio show.
questions.q28: If the chart ranking is bad, then it is simply bad.
questions.q29: Fellow fans are rivals; I would rather there were fewer of them.
questions.q30: I want the whole world to know how good she is.
questions.q31: If my oshi got a boyfriend, I would burn all of her discs.
questions.q32: I hope my oshi never gets married.
questions.q33: If she does not reply to my DM, that is a betrayal of me.
questions.v4a: The best part of following a voice actress is hearing her rescue a role from a terrible show.
questions.v4b: Honestly, as long as she looks good on camera, I could not care less about the performance.
questions.c3a: Before buying merch I think it over three times: is this really worth the price?
questions.c3b: When new merch of hers drops I never check the price - I order first and think later.
questions.c4a: Money I could spend on her is better spent on time and works.
questions.c4b: I will pay real money for every limited edition of hers. It is a matter of attitude.
questions.m4a: Good things should be known by everyone; I never hold back a recommendation.
questions.m4b: I do not want to mention her in public; too many fans actually upsets me.
questions.i3a: Just seeing her on stage makes my day; nothing else matters.
questions.i3b: Showbiz is showbiz. I watch calmly, then make a joke or two.
questions.i4a: Even when she flubs a line or sings off key, I just find it cute.
questions.i4b: Bad craft should be pointed out; liking her and excusing her are different things.
questions.wv1: Her training shows the moment she opens her mouth, and that matters far more than her face.
questions.wv2: I will replay the same clip over and over for a single line of delivery.
questions.wv3: Face first, acting second is a perfectly normal order for me.
questions.wc1: Free-riding is no shame; works deserve to be seen by as many people as possible.
questions.wc2: The best way to support a voice actress is to make her discs and merch sell.
questions.wc3: I do not begrudge the money; limited and first-press editions are never missed.
questions.wm1: When I find something good I cannot help recommending it to everyone, interested or not.
questions.wm2: The moment a recommendation lands feels better than listening ten times.
questions.wm3: I think liking something should stay low-key; there is no need to announce it.
questions.wi1: I almost never criticise her - at most I simply do not praise this one.
questions.wi2: Like is like, but if the work is bad I will say so.
questions.wi3: The moment I see deliberate showbiz moves I sober up and start roasting.
questions.xv1: Her worth should be proven by a cast list, not a photobook.
questions.xv2: Photobooks and live tickets are the things actually worth collecting.
questions.xv3: The better she looks, the harder I fall. I am honest about that.
questions.xc1: The works are free anyway; I do not need to pay for affection.
questions.xc2: My way of following her is remembering every role, not filling a shelf.
questions.xc3: Any affection that money can settle, I will settle with money.
questions.xm1: I clip, I write long posts, and I list her virtues one by one for others.
questions.xm2: I really do not care whether others know her; I just need to like her myself.
questions.xm3: Her name is best mentioned only inside a small circle.
questions.xi1: I cannot say a bad word about her, even if the whole world is attacking her.
questions.xi2: A thick filter is fine by me; I am on her side, period.
questions.xi3: I will call out deliberate showbiz moves even if she is my oshi.
questions.t6: Voice actresses are people and deserve respect.
questions.t7: I have never attacked a voice actress on an anonymous board.
questions.t8: I would be embarrassed if a voice actress read what I wrote.
questions.t9: I did not answer this survey randomly on purpose.
questions.v5a: I can remember a role she played for ten years, and forgot her face long ago.
questions.v5b: My phone is full of her photobooks and event photos.
questions.v6a: Picking what to watch is simple: if she is in the cast list, I open it.
questions.v6b: What matters more to me is whether she does TV shows or photobooks.
questions.c5a: Doujin, raws and second-hand are my main channels; paying is optional.
questions.c5b: Ordering on release day is basic etiquette.
questions.c6a: A sensible fan spends within their means; money does not grow on trees.
questions.c6b: Spending money on someone I like never feels like a loss.
questions.m5a: When I find something good I move it into the group chat so everyone can watch.
questions.m5b: Talking about her inside the group is enough; I do not need to spread it.
questions.m6a: Recommending her is my daily source of joy.
questions.m6b: I rarely bring her up with others; liking is a private matter.
questions.i5a: Whatever she does is right, and there is nothing to discuss.
questions.i5b: I check the facts first, and only then decide whether to speak for her.
questions.i6a: If someone criticises her, my first thought is that I may have misunderstood.
questions.i6b: Criticism and affection can coexist; I never dodge the question.
questions.wv4: The moment the voice starts I know whether the character can be saved.
questions.wv5: Her stage styling excites me more than her acting.
questions.wc4: If I can hear it for free, I will not go out of my way to buy it.
questions.wc5: Buying her disc is the most direct way I express affection.
questions.wm4: I edit the clips I like and share them with fellow fans.
questions.wm5: I prefer following quietly on my own, without joining the discussion.
questions.wi4: One line from her can stay with me for a long time; I do not analyse it.
questions.wi5: Interaction is interaction; I keep a little distance.
questions.xv4: A cast list is her portfolio; everything else is a bonus.
questions.xv5: Her face is persuasive enough on its own.
questions.xc4: My affection does not need to be proven by spending.
questions.xc5: The moment she drops merch, my card is ready.
questions.xm4: I will push her onto anyone still willing to listen.
questions.xm5: The fewer fellow fans, the stronger the sense of ownership.
questions.xi4: She has no flaws in my eyes - I cannot name even one.
questions.xi5: I can hear showbiz phrasing instantly, and I will call it out on the spot.
questions.t10: I buy two copies of her merch: one to keep, one to preach with.
questions.t11: If someone badmouths my oshi, I will remember who they are.
questions.t12: I have never spent a single coin on a voice actress. Not poor - a principle.
questions.t13: When a voice actress has her private life exposed, fans have a right to know.
questions.v7a: A voice actress job is to act with her voice; looks should not enter the evaluation at all.
questions.v7b: Voice actresses are entertainers, so looks and stage presence are fair game for comment.
questions.v8a: How good the performance is has nothing to do with age, face or figure.
questions.v8b: When a character does not match the performer, the audience checks out, and saying so is fine.
questions.c7a: A disc costs a fortune; I would rather spend that money on my life. Liking someone is not a tax.
questions.c7b: If you will not buy the disc, do not demand new releases. That is the unreasonable part.
questions.c8a: Crowdfunding tributes and chart-rigging campaigns are not for me; that turns affection into a vanity project.
questions.c8b: Fan crowdfunding is the most concrete support there is, and those who pay have earned their say.
questions.m7a: The fandom runs on jargon and gatekeeping, so I actively pull newcomers in.
questions.m7b: Newcomers ask the way in and veterans are tired of answering. The coldness has reasons.
questions.m8a: Fellow fans should help each other: group orders, ticket swaps, shared resources are the healthy norm.
questions.m8b: Fellow fans are rivals; on ticket day nobody gives way.
questions.i7a: Even if she is cancelled tomorrow, I will read her own account first instead of following the mob.
questions.i7b: Cancelled is cancelled. However much I like her, the facts stay facts.
questions.i8a: Voice actresses are ordinary people; a private-life slip should not be blown out of proportion.
questions.i8b: Public figures private morals are fair to discuss; whitewashing them for her is the strange part.
questions.wv6: When I judge a voice actress I look at the quality of her credit list first.
questions.wv7: I look at her recent activity and exposure first.
questions.wc6: Limited editions and first-press gimmicks do nothing for me.
questions.wc7: I buy basically every limited edition she releases. Habit, I suppose.
questions.wm6: I joined several fan groups just to talk about her.
questions.wm7: I left every group. Following quietly on my own is easier.
questions.wi6: I basically never have an opinion about what she does.
questions.wi7: I judge what she does for myself, and I do not always agree.
questions.xv6: Going idol is an industry compromise, and I do not like it.
questions.xv7: As long as she gets to be seen on stage, any label works for me.
questions.xc6: I have never bought a single disc, and I still have every right to review her work.
questions.xc7: I am willing to put money into her fan crowdfunding.
questions.xm6: I will carry her merch around and preach to anyone.
questions.xm7: I do not want her to get more famous; once she is, I cannot listen quietly any more.
questions.xi6: She is flawless in my eyes, and I reject every negative word.
questions.xi7: If she is wrong, I will say so; a fan is not her lawyer.
questions.t14: If she were revealed to be dating, I would feel she lied to me.
questions.t15: She owes her fans accountability, including reporting her relationships.
questions.t16: I admit I sometimes fantasise about being part of her life.
